applies_why: The judge text assigns UNDERDETERMINED to the Acts 2:30 issue because the competing loins/seed chains do not force each other, which treats the verse as open between senses.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: I weighed 'That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED' as either forbidding this UNDERDETERMINED finding based on Acts 2:30 not forcing a route, or allowing a chain-level stalemate after weighing multiple verses.
why: The judge's stated ground—'neither chain forces the other'—leaves Acts 2:30 open between the loins-at-depth and Joseph-line readings, when K-S2 says a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand.
